v2_chair1_text: Expand rent control to cover all rental units communitywide
chair2_text: Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units
chair_text_v1: Expand rent control to all rental units with strong tenant protections and just-cause eviction requirements
generated_for: Season-2 carry re-audit of the rent-regulation rev-2 double-barrel split (chair 1 de-barreled and sharpened to universal, all-units coverage). The old chair 1 welded universal rent control + tenant protections + just-cause eviction; the sharpened chair 1 is the maximal position only. All 36 rows were seated on the old broad wording.
discriminator: Chair 1 = rent control extended to cover ALL rental units communitywide (the maximal/universal position). Chair 2 = strengthen EXISTING rent stabilization and extend coverage to MORE units (incremental). A stabilization instrument (RSO cap, AB 1482-style statewide cap with new-construction/SFH exemptions, MA 'Rent Stabilization Act' / 'lift the ban' local-option bills) proves the pro DIRECTION and the stabilization MAGNITUDE — that is chair 2, not chair 1. Direction-only evidence (general tenant protection, eviction, organizing, rental assistance, affordable-housing, land trusts) under-determines the chair -> blank, per CLAUDE.md ('the honest alternative to a guessed chair is a blank spoke').
decision: Correct in-place on Season 1 / rev 1 (all 36 answers are stamped Season 1, rev 1). A wrong chair is wrong in the open season too, so moves and blanks apply now and the corrected chair carries into Season 2 when it opens with rev 2 pinned. Blank = DELETE the answer (value CHECK is 1-5, no null sentinel) AND delete the matching politician_context row, since that reasoning was written to justify the rejected chair-1 claim (answer-delete context decision).
borderline_note: Rows flagged borderline are genuine judgment calls; read the sources before committing. carry_1 borderlines lean 1 but the cited action is thin (re-source recommended). move_2 borderlines have only a bare 'supports rent control' statement with no magnitude — placed at 2 as the nearest evidenced chair, not blanked, because they still name rent control as the instrument-class.
resourced_pass: 2026-08-30 — the 7 direction-only blanks were re-sourced (one WebSearch/WebFetch agent each, same primary-instrument bar). Result: 2 -> chair 1 (Fielder, Huang, both via a Costa-Hawkins-repeal / 'universal rent control' platform), 2 -> chair 2 (Chan File 220636, Walton File 240822, both extend-to-more-units votes/co-sponsorships), 3 confirmed blank (Hall, Hettleman, Zhang — no qualifying primary rent-control instrument). The 6 borderlines from the first pass were accepted as written and not re-sourced.

rows.name: Ayanna Pressley
rows.why: Cited instruments are the Rent Relief Act (HR 4226, a renter tax credit), 'backing local rent stabilization', and the Affordable Housing Act (community land trusts). Stabilization + tenant assistance, not universal all-units control.

rows.name: Caroline Torosis
rows.why: Two-term Santa Monica Rent Control Board member and SMRR-aligned voice; Santa Monica runs one of the broadest municipal rent-control regimes. Institutionally the maximal-control camp, but the cited action ('urged Council to draft an ordinance expanding renter protections') is vague — re-source to a specific broad-coverage act.

rows.name: Chynah Tyler
rows.why: Co-sponsor of H.1304 ('lift the ban on rent stabilization'); restoring local rent-control authority. Stabilization / local-option = chair 2.

rows.name: Cindy Allen
rows.why: Statement only: 'support stricter forms of local rent control.' Reads as strengthen-existing; no all-units/universal claim and no instrument. Nearest evidenced chair is 2.

rows.name: Connie Chan
rows.why: Re-sourced: co-sponsor of SF Board of Supervisors File 220636 (Peskin, 2022), a charter amendment placing rent control on all residential units in projects that exceed new density/height limits — extends coverage to MORE (Costa-Hawkins-exempt) units, conditional on new development. Extend-to-more-units = chair 2, not a universal cap. (Prior Union-At-Home / anti-eviction citations were not rent control.)

rows.name: Dan Hall
rows.why: Re-sourced, confirmed blank: Santa Monica councilmember. Own site says only 'fight for the strongest renter protections' (no instrument/magnitude); one recorded act is a 6-0 eviction-protection vote (not rent control); a news-reported line about 'organizing against threats to our Rent Control law' is defensive activism, not a primary instrument. Leans chair-2 direction but clears no primary-instrument bar.

rows.name: Daniel J. Hunt
rows.why: Co-sponsor of H.1304 ('lift the ban'); restoring local rent-control authority via stabilization. Chair 2.

rows.name: David Chiu

rows.name: Ellen Zhang

Platform lists 'rent control' as one bare bullet in a Tenant Bill of Rights with no magnitude; her actual housing plan is supply-side, and Wisconsin bans local rent control. Cannot distinguish chair 1 from chair 2.

rows.name: Shamann Walton
rows.why: Re-sourced: recorded (unanimous) vote for SF File 240822 (Peskin, Oct 2024) moving the rent-control cutoff from 1979 to 1994, extending stabilization to ~16k more units (contingent on Prop 33).
